title: Drop 1
summary: A small, real-world product drop to test demand, sourcing, positioning, and fulfilment without overbuilding.
why: Use a constrained commerce experiment to learn whether SIndustries can turn sourcing, positioning, and fulfilment into a repeatable revenue motion.
successCriteria: A complete product drop runs end to end with clear demand, fulfilment effort, margin, and customer-response evidence.

title: Social content
summary: Short-form public signal to build distribution, sharpen narrative, and learn what people respond to.
why: Build a low-friction distribution loop while SIndustries is still forming, so public feedback can shape the company before the model fully resolves.
successCriteria: A repeatable posting cadence produces clear evidence about which topics, formats, and claims earn useful attention.

title: Product Market Scans
summary: Recurring scans for gaps, pricing windows, underserved niches, and first-drop candidates.
why: Keep opportunity discovery systematic instead of relying on memory or sporadic inspiration.
successCriteria: Scans regularly produce prioritized candidates with evidence, constraints, and a clear next action.

title: Plano model routing
summary: Local model routing for cheaper, faster, more autonomous agent work across routine operations.
why: Reduce cost and latency for recurring agent work while keeping stronger models available for judgment-heavy tasks.
successCriteria: Routine workflows route reliably through appropriate models with observable quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs.

title: NZ Personal Banking App
summary: A visibility layer for household spending, budget drift, and real-time financial control.
why: Explore whether household money visibility can become a useful product wedge for New Zealand banking realities.
successCriteria: The concept has a narrowed user problem, credible data-access path, and a testable prototype scope.

title: Roadmapping Scenarios App
summary: A scenario-driven planning surface for comparing paths, trade-offs, and sequencing decisions.
why: Make strategic planning more concrete by turning options, constraints, and trade-offs into comparable scenarios.
successCriteria: A prototype helps compare at least two meaningful paths and makes sequencing decisions clearer.
